title: MERS-CoV, South Korea, 2015
publisher: European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control, Epidemic Intelligence and Response section; transfer to R and documentation by Bertrand Sudre
purpose: Teaching, as the package states; neither the final investigation nor a complete transmission chain.
licence: NONE STATED for the data, checked 2026-11-11. Package code: MIT (GitHub), GPL (>= 2) (CRAN 1.9.0).
licenceDecision: Used for teaching, the purpose the package states, by the Fieldwork practitioner's decision of 2026-11-11: "Our use case for these worked examples is for teaching so that fits MERS Korea purpose". A judgement about use, not a licence grant.
limits: Dates are per case, collected in the outbreak's first weeks: case-level timeliness (onset to report, onset to diagnosis) can be computed for the 135 cases with an onset date; a 7-1-7 review of the outbreak as one event cannot, since no early response action dates are held.
dt_death is empty for the 152 cases not recorded as dead.
The contacts are probable links, as the package says, not a confirmed transmission chain.

data/mers_korea_2015_facilities.csv.joinsOn: loc_hosp, as the line list writes it
data/mers_korea_2015_facilities.csv.licence: ODbL-1.0, for the OpenStreetMap coordinates it carries; (c) OpenStreetMap contributors

sources.OpenStreetMap: 10 rows (one a street, not the facility), read through Nominatim lookups on 2026-11-12
sources.Wikidata: 2 rows (Hallym University Dongtan Sacred Heart Hospital, Q16099199), CC0
sources.identification: The hospitals named by the Korean government on 7 June 2015, and by Gangdong-gu on 1 July 2015

limits: loc_hosp is defined by the package as the hospital where a case was hospitalized; its counts follow where cases were exposed. A map of it shows hospitals named for cases.
"Hallym University Medical Center" names a network of hospitals; Dongtan is the most likely, marked low confidence.
Asan Seoul Clinic is placed at the middle of its street, and 365 Seoul Yeollin Clinic not at all: neither is mapped.
